newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mixed, erasing earlier gain.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mixed, erasing earlier gain.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed mixed on Thursday after the yen's gains against the dollar during Tokyo trading erased the bullish mood in early morning, traders said.
Prices ranged from 70 yen lower to 80 yen higher, with benchmark November 1997 contract down 70 yen at 14,140 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 33,362 lots.

All contracts rallied at the opening, as the firmer CBOT corn market overnight encouraged local investors to buy, traders said. "Active fresh buying emerged from individual investors at the opening. But the yen's gains later erased the momentum," a brokerage trader said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.72 per bushel at 0850 GMT, compared with Wednesday's closing price of $2.71-3/4.
The spot November contract of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $6.91-3/4 at 0850 GMT, compared with $6.92-3/4 at Wednesday's close.
